M O R E   M A I L ! !


 November, 1994      Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -
 Terry Thomas.........03    04
 Daphne Shiels........07    11
 Glenn Atkins.........13    14
 David Wornham........15    17
 Cristian Secara......22    30
 Malcolm Goodman......32    39
 Chris Oliver.........41    47

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From Terry Thomas, GWENT

Dear Ron,

Sorry to hear that I cannot run
the PC version of OUTLET on my
5.25" drive.

If I get a 3.5" drive system can
I then run OUTLET because I have
an SVGA monitor and an upgrade
to a 640K. Perhaps you can give
me some advice in OUTLETTERS.

What is the difference between
VGA and SVGA and other monitors?

As always, your advice is very
welcome. Thank you.

              Terry Thomas

Brian Cavers to Terry Thomas

If you get a 3.5" drive it MUST
be a high-density (HD) drive to
run OUTLET. These are now the
most common so you will not have
any trouble getting one.They are
often listed as 1.44Mb drives
which is their capacity when
formatted by MS-DOS for the PC.

SVGA can provide a higher resol-
ution (number of dots on-screen)
giving higher quality than VGA.
However, this is only evident if
the program you are running uses
the higher screen modes. To run
an SVGA monitor you need a video
display card in your PC that can
handle SVGA. SVGA includes VGA
modes so all VGA graphics will
be OK on an SVGA system.

OUTLET only needs VGA to run the
main magazine and most programs
but there may be occasional
software that needs SVGA or runs
better with SVGA.

VGA display goes up to a screen
that is 640 dots wide by 480
dots high with any 16 colours
from a palette of over a quarter
of a million - OR - a screen
that is 320 dots by 200 but with
any 256 colours from the quarter
of a million.

SVGA can have a screen 640 x 480
or 800 x 600 or 1024 x 768 each
with up to 16 million colours!
However,you need the right card,
drivers and video memory, e.g.,
1024 x 768 x 16 million needs
2Mb of video memory.

For general use I'd recommend
SVGA. You can always add video
memory and special drivers if
you later get some high-powered
graphic program and specifically
want extra quality.

                         Brian

From: Daphne Shiels, VICTORIA



Dear Chezron,

YES PLEASE! Start sending me the
PC version of OUTLET - the first
four issues were wonderful!

I usually receive each issue by
the 11th or 12th. I cannot be
sure exactly because we do not
go to the postbox every day but
it always arrives by the 15th
except for one issue a couple of
years ago. That was more likely
the result of a postage problem
than anything to do with you I
imagine. You have always been
incredibly reliable.


The computer club to which I
belong, has its meetings on the
third Wednesday of each month
and the current issue of OUTLET
always seems to arrive just
before then so that I can take
along the latest news from
England. Since none of us have
magazine subscriptions any more
(the postage was astronomical),
we rely on OUTLET for the latest
information.

We only have about 30 members
and only about 12 who are close
enough to attend meetings,but we
all still enjoy our Sinclairs.
We have several QL's and even
two ZX81's in the group. Most of
us now have PC's and have found
the Lunter emulator superb.


That is why I was so interested
in the program I was talking
about in the last letter I wrote
to you. There was some informat-
ion on the last page of... now I
have lost the piece of paper I
wrote it on. It was about an add
on program for the emulator to
do with loading microdrive files
and I think it was Issue 82.


I found the piece of paper! See
Spectrum OUTLET 83, last page of
OUTVERTS...


   "CATLOADER for PC Lunter
   emulator for pseudo-
   microdrive operation. Only
   `2 from Chezron Software."


As always, I look forward to
each issue of OUTLET. Keep up
the good work. I hope you know
how much interest and pleasure
you give to your subscribers.

  Hope the world is
    being kind to you all,

      Regards from Australia,

              Daphne











Ron Cavers to Daphne Shiels


Glad to hear that you enjoyed
OUTLET on the PC so much - many
thanks for your subscription -
the enclosed issues will bring
you up-to-date.

I'm surprised (and pleased!) to
learn that you receive your
monthly disk so early - I'd
imagined that it was taking a
couple of weeks at least to get
there but it looks as though it
only takes a few days (I usually
post them out between the 3rd
and the 6th each month) so the
news you take to the local comp-
uter club isn't so far behind
after all.


Sorry for the confusion re the
Lunter emulator - I should have
realised that you were talking
about CATLOADER. Since the emul-
ator can be set up for pseudo-
microdrive operation, Brian
converted our CATLOADER program
to help with file handling.

                      Ron













From Glenn M. Atkins, HAMPTON

I've decided to postpone my ac-
quisition of a Pentium-based PC
to a later date - primarily, I
think, to wait until the price
comes down a bit - which I know
it will. I'm a bit dubious about
upgrading a 486 to Pentium tech-
nology as you may want to in the
future. It's my understanding
that, provided your PC has the
correct socket on the mother-
board, you can install what's
codenamed a "P24T", otherwise
known as a Pentium Overdrive
chip. I suspect that it's the
equivalent of having a 386 with
a maths co-processor (387). As
it's not even available yet, we
can only speculate.
                          Glenn

Brian Cavers to Glenn Atkins

The P24T was supposed to be due
at the end of this year but I
haven't seen it advertised any-
where yet. Mind you, I heard it
may cost `800 to `1000!

                    Brian

From David Wornham,DROITWICH SPA

Dear Ron & Brian,

Alright, I admit it! Since conv-
erting my OUTLET subs to the PC
version (which I hasten to add I
very much appreciate), because I
still use my Spectrum, I have
missed your useful routines,etc,
for that machine. I therefore
forward a cheque for back issues
and subscription!

Now that I am back in your Spec-
trum membership, I have a query.
I wish to convert DATA files
from SAM to Spectrum +D. I have
tried your SAMTOD from Issue 46
but find that it rejects SAM
DATA files, stating: "NOT SAME
CODE OR A SAM SCREEN$".

Although I appreciate that this
is a SAM query, as it also
concerns the +D, others may find
it useful (and I am sure that
you will find it simple) I
request,nevertheless, that you
try to assist.

As a matter of interest, I find
that SAM accepts +D DATA files
but that lately has been corr-
upting the latter half when
loading a large DATA file using
DIM A$(187,160). I am sure that
this did not occur before when I
have loaded the same size +D
DATA files to SAM. My SAM (now
upgraded to 512K - could this be
the cause?) appears otherwise to
work perfectly.
                   David Wornham

Brian Cavers to David Wornham

The SAM Coupe stores variables
a different way to the Spectrum
and I'm not surprised you cannot
transfer them. In fact, I am
AMAZED that you say you used to
be able to load Spectrum DATA
string arrays direct into the
SAM! I try never to say never or
impossible - there may be a way
- but the only solution I can
see at the moment is a bit of
BASIC to convert to code for the
transfer and then convert back.
This would need customising for
the particular array but an
elaborate program might adjust
itself I guess. Here is a simple
method you can adjust manually
to suit...


This assumes A$(187,160) already
DIMmed.. and at least 5K free.
It can be used on SAM to send to
Spectrum or vice versa but
adjust the SAVE syntax for +D..

   5 CLEAR 60000
  10 LET S=60001:LET E=65000
  15 LET A=S: LET F=1
  20 FOR X=1 TO 187
  30  FOR Y=1 TO 160
  40   POKE A,CODE A$(X,Y)
  50   LET A=A+1
  60   IF A=E THEN GOSUB 500
  70  NEXT Y
  80 NEXT X
  90 GOSUB 500
 100 STOP
 500 SAVE "TEMP." + STR$ F CODE
     S,5000
 510 LET F=F+1 : LET A=S
 520 RETURN

Here is a program to load the
data sent by the previous
program from the other machine.
On +D, alter the syntax and use
SAMTOD first to convert from SAM
to +D...
   3 CLEAR 60000
   5 DIM A$(187,160)
  10 LET S=60001:LET E=65000
  15 LET A=S: LET F=1: GOSUB 500
  20 FOR X=1 TO 187
  30  FOR Y=1 TO 160
  40   LET A$(X,Y)=CHR$ PEEK A
  50   LET A=A+1
  60   IF A=E THEN GOSUB 500
  70  NEXT Y
  80 NEXT X
  90 STOP
 500 LOAD "TEMP"+STR$ F CODE S
 510 LET F=F+1: LET A=S
 520 RETURN

You can no doubt improve on the
above, for example, on SAM you
might use MEM$. Note also that
there seems to be a bug in SAM-
TOD. Make sure you have the S on
the end of the LOAD line if you
are loading a "SAMTODDED" code
file into +D. The S is the load
address of course. Without it, I
found the code did not load to
the right address (I don't know
WHERE it went!) although the
address looks OK in the CAT!

Use a similar method for numeric
arrays. Positive integers from 0
to 255 can be POKEd directly to
memory. Positive integers from 0
to 65535 need a double POKE and
so on. Negative numbers and/or
fractions need some more thought
to convert!

A much better way would have
been to use OPENTYPE files but
if I remember correctly, it is
not possible to load +D OPENTYPE
files in to SAM via MASTERDOS or
MASTERDOS into +D (don't know if
BETADOS helps).

Anyway, hopefully the above will
give you some ideas.

                        Brian

From Cristian Secara, BUCHAREST


Here are some comments about
OUTLET 85...


1. Why do you say you cannot
make a working copy of Tasword
+3 for the B: drive? I checked
it...

I insert the master disc in
Drive A:; load "RUN"; exit to
main menu; change the program's
drive switch to B: (SS+B) and
select the "Save Tasword" option
(T). When prompted,I put a blank
disc in drive A; (and ENTER). It
copies OK. After this I RESET my
Speccy.


Now this disc (the same format
for both drives - my situation)
is inserted in Drive B:; load
"RUN"and that's it!For different
formats, copy the freshly-saved
Tasword program still in A: to a
disc in B: using BASIC's COPY
command). The new copy will use
by default Drive B:. So?? Be
sure to use the "Save Tasword"
option only after changing the
menu's drive switch. However,
with the program in the B:
drive, the "Save Tasword" option
cannot be used so it seems the
reverse situation cannot exist
(I mean to make back a working
copy for A: from the program
installed for B:). As a "REM" in
the BASIC tells me, my Tasword
+3 seems to be Version 2.01.


2. About a letter from Tony
Wilson for information only (if
someone else asks): the +2A/+3
BASIC'S COPY command (located at
#20CE or #223B in ROM1 depending
on the version) uses the PIXEL
ADDRESS (sub)routine (located at
#22AA in ROM3) used by POINT and
PLOT commands where a "PLOT 0,0"
is on the 22nd line, not on the
24th. For this reason, the last
2*8 lines are not calculated and
cannot be Plotted.

On my computer I have modified
the ROM1. At present, COPY
calls a modified routine (very
short in fact),very similar to
the PIXEL ADDRESS but extended
to 24 lines that now exist in an
empty zone inside the same ROM1.


I also installed Art Studio for
my Citizen 120D+ printer. So,now
I can use all dump options. The
original routines of this
program are very clever but the
aspect ratio is a bit worse in
some circumstances (depends on
the printer's chosen graphic
mode - I have no idea if using
another printer). Tony Wilson
wanted a program that can make a
copy on the left/right part of a
paper sheet. Art Studio with the
printer installed can make this
(left, centre or right printing)

I also modified the CAT routine,
because on any original +3 (all
issues), if there are more than
64 directory entries (usually
with 720K drives, unlikely or


impossible for 180K ones) only
the first 64 titles are
displayed - free space follows
immediately).

3. It seems that before printing
something, your editor make a
soft-reset to a printer (ESC @).
Is this so useful? For example,
just after power-on I send to my
printer codes for (a) slashed 0,
(b)6 lines skip over perforation
and (c) 1/8" line spacing (for
listings, not letters). For the
first two there are no hard
switches to do that. I've listed
something from your disc (using
the "P" option then "+3
Centronics") and my printer was
again just like after power-on,
all soft settings erased.


This is no problem for me and
not important at this moment. I
think there must be some BASIC
line(s) that can be modified (no
time for that now) but I guess
that this may create some con-
fusion (to the user rather than
the printer!).

Maybe you already know this but
type the following(+2A/+3 only)


 10 COPY EXP
 20 STOP
 30 POKE 23760,249
 40 FOR X=0 TO 500: NEXT X
 50 GO TO 10

[In line 30, 249 is the code for
the keyword RANDOMIZE - Ed]


Now, RUN 30. Very quickly press
simultaneously "C, "J" and "L"
and wait a moment. What's the
use of this? To +3's equipped
with the faulty ROM (version 4.0
on test menu) the colour speed
cannot be changed and you can
only RESET the computer;to +2A's
or +3's with the fixed ROM
(Version 4.1 on test menu), by
pressing "P" or "O" the speed
can be increased/decreased and
with "Q" return to BASIC.


23760 is the start of BASIC plus
5. This is the memory position
of the "EXP". I can see no other
easy way to type"COPY RANDOMIZE"
[the POKE replaces the keyword
EXP with RANDOMIZE - Ed]


For me it's amazing how you have
the ability to have made so many
issues of OUTLET on so many
formats - to read letters and
respond to many of them and to
check programs. Do you ever go
to sleep?

Keep up the good work!

                    Cristi


Brian Cavers to Cristian Secara

I'll take your word for it about
getting Tasword +3 to work with
the B drive as default! I know I
tried all the obvious things but
without success! Thanks for the
solution!

Our printer routines usually
clear the printer of any codes
first because many codes will
cause a print out to fail. For
example, our TABLOID print has
several changes to spacing and
may not position correctly if
certain codes have already been
sent. It is a good policy to
"clear the slate"before proceed-
ing or how can you tell if there
will not be some conflict?


For example, suppose one OUTLET
program prints out some text in
large characters in italics and
leaves your printer in that same
mode. Now you try to print some
text in another program which is
formatted to exactly fit an A4
sheet with 64 characters on one
line. The second program sets
the left margin to 8 but does
not clear any existing codes. It
will print in large italics and
the entire page will be wrongly
formatted.

Yes, I did sleep once - I fell
asleep at the keyboard. It was a
Christmas treat. I woke guiltily
at 4am and typed in the January
editorial during breakfast.
                  Brian, 7.30pm

From Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS

I would just like to add my two
pennyworth to the debate on
pricing that has appeared rec-
ently in your columns. Some time
ago, I gave some thought to
buying a PC. So, I went out and
bought some mags to read in
order to get an idea of prices
and specifications. It soon
became apparent that I would
also need to learn some jargon
if I wasn't to make any expens-
ive mistakes. So, for about four
months I did my homework and
resigned myself to the idea that
whichever PC I opted for would
be 'plus VAT'. It also appeared
that any software/hardware would
also have 17.5% added.


Everyone I spoke to advised me
that buying by mail order was
cheaper than purchasing from a
retail outlet, and a check
around seemed to confirm this.
My conclusion was that because
PCs are predominantly aimed at
the business sector, that this
iniquitous VAT was being added
to what was, in my view, all
that the PC might be really
worth.

Anyway, I narrowed the field
down to two probable suppliers,
and was about to place my order,
when I noted an advert in the
evening paper from a local
retailer, offering me my ideal
computer at a tax-inclusive
price.


I visited the shop and had a
convincing demo of the PC, and
then asked why they could offer
this machine at this lower
price. "Simple!", said the
salesman, "We cater for the
domestic user, who wants an
all-inclusive price."

That all-inclusive price saved
me about `200 compared with
mail order pricing which I think
confirms my earlier suspicions.

So now I have a 486SX/25(running
at 33Mhz), 450Mb hard drive, 1Mb
accelerated SVGA graphics, a
double speed CD ROM, a Sound-
Blaster-compatible card, a non-
interlaced monitor, plus a two
year extended warranty.


In addition, I have the option
over the first few months, to
exchange any of the cards for
alternative boards, and paying
only for the difference in price
between the exchange units. I
don't know of (m)any other
suppliers who offer the same
service.


Having bought the PC I then
decided to get something to run
on it, and felt that 'Encarta
94' was a good start. So once
again I checked around 'the
jungle' for the best price. This
varied from `80 including VAT
down to `39 + p&p + VAT (some
difference!), and naturally went
for the cheaper price.


A quick phone call resulted in
next-day delivery but I was
horrified to see that I had been
charged `4.75 + VAT for p&p. On
querying this with the supplier
I was told this was a standard
charge for CD ROMS - even though
the postage only amounted to
`1.20 plus a jiffy bag. Yet a
further example of business
oriented pricing? Even so, I
still finished up with the
cheapest 'bottom line' price,
so I felt reasonably (!) happy.

Then it was off to look for some
books to help me.I just couldn't
believe most of the prices being
asked for them. These I felt
were out of all proportion to
the real value of the books that


I looked at, and once more that
even stronger suspicion about
prices being aimed at the
business user. How anyone can
justify `15 for a book that has
less than 400 pages is beyond
me - especially one that is
supposed to have sold many
100,000 copies. Exploitation is
the word that springs readily to
mind.


Then there is the question of
software. How can a supplier
give several programs (sorry,
applications) with a suggested
retail of several hundred pounds
free(!?) with their computer(s),
unless the computer and/or the
software is grossly overpriced?


As far as games are concerned, I
consider `20+ is excessive, and
in the event that I decide that
I want a game, then I will
obtain mine from 'alternative'
sources until such time as
prices become more realistic.

Perhaps someone can explain?
Until then I will remain firmly
convinced that I am being ripped
off.

In case anyone out there is
looking for a reasonably priced
supplier of PCs, I can strongly
recommend: Pudsey Computers, 161
Richardshaw Lane, Pudsey, Leeds,
LS28 6AA. Telephone:0532 360650.

               Malcolm Goodman
.

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Goodman


While searching for a good book
on QUICK BASIC programming, I
remember seeing one that was a
very hefty volume - perhaps 2"
across the spine. However, when
I opened it up, the pages were
relatively thick and there were
only about 400 to 500 pages and
each one was printed in a thick
largish print that was spread
out amongst many space-wasting
diagrams. The actual substance
of the text could probably have
been summarised in a hundred
pages. The price was about `40.
It wasn't just the weight of the
thing that made me heft it back
on its shelf rather quickly!

I always recommend the MICROSOFT
QUICKBASIC BIBLE published by
the Waite Group (reference is
ISBN 1-55615-262-0). This is
excellent both as tutorial and
reference but is an awful `27.95
and you may have to search many
a bookshop to find a copy!

If you get further into QBASIC
(as supplied with MS-DOS) then
you may eventually want to buy
QUICK BASIC which has many extra
editorial features but also one
can compile the programs into
stand-alone EXE files. It too
has to be searched for and may
cost over `100!
                       -Brian

From Chris Oliver, STAFFS

   SPECTRES in the SPECTRUM?
           or "UFOs"
 (UNIDENTIFIED FILING OBJECTS)
Here is a true tale of the un-
expected and unexplained to
chill your spine as you sit by
the fire on a dark winter's
night. Yes, I have had a visit-
ation from a "Phantom File"! It
happened when I was using the
infallible OUTLET utility CAT-
LOADER to copy a batch of files
from disc to disc. I'd selected
the required files and set it
running, left the room (to visit
the bathroom, if you really need
to know!)and returned to find an
extra file had been copied in
between the ones I'd selected.
Strange!

Even stranger, the apparition
did not appear to be on the disc
I was copying from! So where had
it come from?? There was nobody
else in the house at the time,
so human interference can be
ruled out.

    DEMONS in the DIRECTORY?
The catalogue of the disc I was
copying-to lists the ghost file
as "Letters". A common enough
file name you may think, but
actually one which I have never
used myself. So my curiosity was
aroused: The enhanced CAT
(FULLCAT from OUTLET #79) tells
me that "Letters" is a Basic
file occupying 54 sectors, auto-
running from line 1, with a
length of 27156 bytes.


All that sounds logical enough,
so let's have a look at these
mysterious letters!

Full of anticipation and not
knowing what to expect, I loaded
"Letters". Perhaps some Runes
from beyond the ROM would appear
or maybe just a pack of pixilat-
ed pixels or a set of spiritual
sprites? No,nothing so exciting,
just the report "O.K. G+DOS,0:1"
which is the sort of error
report one gets when the autorun
line number is beyond the last
line of the program. Humph!

So next let's LIST the program
to see what's occupying that 27k
of Basic area..... What do you
think?Nothing!Absolutely nothing
showed up! - a true ghost-file!

As you may imagine, severe
frustration is starting to set
in, so out come the 'tools-of-
the-trade' to see just what is
what - first, a disassembler to
scan through exactly what, if
anything, is actually there:-

There's not a lot except for
what seems to be two well-spaced
copies of the disc directory
file. Not very exciting!

So where had the alien come
from? Intense scrutiny of all
the discs in use was called for.
I used SHIFTER (from OUTLET #67)
which allows one to examine
every byte on every sector of a
disc, and also gives a CAT which
lists even the ERASED files on a
disc.

First I examined the source disc
- Aha! - four ERASED files
materialised - but none had a
filename remotely like"Letters".
Every sector of the directory
file was examined, but no trace
could be found of "Letters".


The disc containing the transfer
program was the next candidate,
but again, not a trace of a file
named "Letters"!

On to the target disc now, and
yes, there is the file "Letters"
in the directory, as expected,
and it indicates that it is a
Basic file of 54 sectors(nothing
new so far!)starting on Track 49
Sector 3.


Track 49? On a 40-track disc???

Stumped!!

Anyone got any ideas on how to
examine a non-existent file,
which lives on a non-existent
sector? Replies please to:

         Chris Oliver,
        The Funny Farm,
        Care of OUTLET.

Brian Cavers to Chris Oliver

Well, if the 40-track drive is
double-sided then it has 40
tracks on each side but it still
would not make sense because
they are numbered 0 to 39 on
Side 1 and 128 to 167 on Side 2!
However, knowing some of the
quirks in the DOS, it may really
mean Track 14 on Side 2 (I make
that equal to 141??!!). If you
still have the disk,try(BETADOS)

    LOAD @ 1,49,1,30001,54
 or LOAD @ 1,49,1,30001,141

Then PEEK through memory from
30001 to 57156 to see if it has
netted anything!
                       Brian.

## Letters (2)

M O R E   M A I L ! !

November, 1994      Page Reply

How to write to us...02     - Terry Thomas.........03    04 Daphne Shiels........07    11 Glenn Atkins.........13    14 David Wornham........15    17 Cristian Secara......22    30 Malcolm Goodman......32    39 Chris Oliver.........41    47

PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE! Text is accepted in any form for OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files (say which),typed or handwritten letters. However, PLEASE send us a textfile if possible so your letter needn't be typed again! The easiest for us to edit are Tasword 2 files with the right margin set at 32 but a textfile in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be parts of your letter you do not wish published but we always use our discretion anyway. Letters may also be edited for clarity and length... Please ask if you welcome direct correspondence from other OUTLET readers and we will publish your full address.

From Terry Thomas, GWENT

Dear Ron,

Sorry to hear that I cannot run the PC version of OUTLET on my 5.25" drive.

If I get a 3.5" drive system can I then run OUTLET because I have an SVGA monitor and an upgrade to a 640K. Perhaps you can give me some advice in OUTLETTERS.

What is the difference between VGA and SVGA and other monitors?

As always, your advice is very welcome. Thank you.

 ```text
  50   LET A=A+1
  60   IF A=E THEN GOSUB 500
  70  NEXT Y

  90 GOSUB 500
 ```

 другой машины. На +D измените синтаксис и

 ```text
  10 LET S=60001:LET E=65000
  15 LET A=S: LET F=1: GOSUB 500
  20 FOR X=1 TO 187
  30  FOR Y=1 TO 160

  50   LET A=A+1
  60   IF A=E THEN GOSUB 500
  70  NEXT Y

  90 STOP

 510 LET F=F+1: LET A=S
 520 RETURN
 ```

Всю суть текста можно было бы запросто уложить страниц в сто. Цена составляла около £40. И не только тяжесть фолианта заставила меня поскорее водрузить его обратно на полку!

## ПРИЗРАКИ в SPECTRUM? или «НЛО» (НЕОПОЗНАННЫЕ ЛЕТАЮЩИЕ ОБЪЕКТЫ / ФАЙЛЫ)

Вот вам правдивая история о неожиданном и необъяснимом, от которой стынет кровь в жилах, пока вы сидите у камина тёмной зимней ночью. Да-да, меня навестил «Файл-Призрак»! Это случилось, когда я использовал безотказную утилиту CAT-LOADER от OUTLET, чтобы скопировать пачку файлов с диска на диск. Я выбрал нужные файлы, запустил процесс, вышел из комнаты (в туалет, если вам так уж интересно!) и, вернувшись, обнаружил, что между выбранными мною файлами скопировался один лишний. Странно!

Что ещё страннее — этого призрака, похоже, вообще не было на диске, с которого я копировал! Откуда же он взялся?? В доме в тот момент больше никого не было, так что вмешательство человека можно исключить.

### DEMONS in the DIRECTORY?

Каталог диска, на который я копировал, отображает файл-призрак как "Letters". Вполне обычное имя файла, скажете вы, но дело в том, что я сам его никогда не использовал. Так что моё любопытство разгорелось не на шутку: расширенный CAT (FULLCAT из OUTLET #79) сообщает мне, что "Letters" — это Basic-файл, занимающий 54 сектора, с автозапуском со строки 1 и длиной 27156 байт.

Всё это звучит вполне логично, так что давайте взглянем на эти загадочные письма!

Полный предвкушения и не зная, чего ожидать, я загрузил "Letters". Может, появятся какие-нибудь руны из глубин ROM, или просто кучка пикселей, или выводок спиритических спрайтов? Нет, ничего настолько захватывающего — лишь отчёт "O.K. G+DOS,0:1", то есть то самое сообщение об ошибке, которое получаешь, когда номер строки автозапуска превышает номер последней строки программы. Хм!

Давайте тогда посмотрим листинг программы (LIST), чтобы выяснить, что же занимает эти 27 Кб бейсик-области... И как вы думаете? Ничего! Не появилось ровным счётом ничего! — истинный файл-призрак!

Как нетрудно догадаться, на смену интересу пришло сильное раздражение, поэтому в ход пошёл профессиональный инструментарий, чтобы разобраться, что к чему. Первым делом — дизассемблер, чтобы досконально просканировать, что же там вообще есть:

Там не так уж много всего, за исключением того, что выглядит как две разнесённые копии файла каталога диска. Не слишком-то увлекательно!

Так откуда же взялся этот пришелец? Потребовалось тщательнейшее обследование всех используемых дисков. Я задействовал SHIFTER (из OUTLET #67), который позволяет исследовать каждый байт каждого сектора диска, а также выводит CAT со списком даже СТЁРТЫХ (ERASED) файлов.

Сначала я проверил исходный диск — ага! — материализовались четыре СТЁРТЫХ файла, но ни один из них и близко не назывался "Letters". Был изучен каждый сектор файла каталога, но никаких следов "Letters" обнаружить не удалось.

Следующим кандидатом стал диск с программой копирования, но опять же — ни единого следа файла с именем "Letters"!

Переходим к целевому диску, и да, в каталоге, как и ожидалось, есть файл "Letters", и там указано, что это Basic-файл на 54 сектора (пока ничего нового!), начинающийся на дорожке 49, в секторе 3.

Дорожка 49? На 40-дорожечном диске???

Полный тупик!!

Есть у кого-нибудь идеи, как исследовать несуществующий файл, живущий в несуществующем секторе? Ответы присылайте по адресу:

```text
         Chris Oliver,
        The Funny Farm,
        Care of OUTLET.
```

### Brian Cavers to Chris Oliver

Что ж, если этот 40-дорожечный дисковод двухсторонний, то у него по 40 дорожек на каждой стороне, но это всё равно лишено смысла, поскольку они нумеруются от 0 до 39 на стороне 1 и от 128 до 167 на стороне 2! Однако, зная некоторые причуды DOS, это на самом деле может означать дорожку 14 на стороне 2 (у меня получается 141??!!). Если диск всё ещё у вас, попробуйте (BETADOS):

```text
    LOAD @ 1,49,1,30001,54
 or LOAD @ 1,49,1,30001,141
```

А затем проверьте память с помощью PEEK от 30001 до 57156 — вдруг что-нибудь да выловилось!

Brian.
